system.name: Vector-HaSH+ (multi-region brain model, M5)
system.one_liner: Grid cells, hippocampus and non-grid sensory cortex form a memory circuit feeding an RNN policy, trained by RL on a T-maze evidence task to compare grid-cell codes.

content.variant_note: four lettered panels: prior circuit (A), proposed circuit with numbered links (B), joint vs disjoint grid-code example (C), T-maze RL loop (D)
content.argues: Grid cells that jointly encode position and evidence, inside a hippocampal memory circuit feeding an RNN policy, are the model component under test in a T-maze RL task.
content.subject: A brain-circuit model (grid cells, hippocampus, non-grid sensory EC, RNN policy) and the T-maze task it is trained on.

lessons.what_to_learn: Keep one colour per variable or region in both the circuit panel and the task-environment panel, and number the circuit's links to give the computation order. Show a toy trajectory on small state-space tiles to contrast two coding schemes.
lessons.suits: Neuroscience-inspired or modular architectures where a circuit, a coding scheme and a task environment must be tied together in one overview.

summary: The paper builds a multi-region brain model, Vector-HaSH+, in which grid cells, hippocampus and non-grid sensory entorhinal cortex form a memory circuit that feeds an RNN policy trained by reinforcement learning on a virtual T-maze evidence task. Figure 1 is a four-panel composite. A redraws the earlier Vector-HaSH circuit with torus-shaped grid modules, a hippocampal band, a sensory band and an arrow key for fixed versus plastic links. B rewires it with pos, evi, MLP and RNN boxes and links numbered (1) to (6). C contrasts joint and disjoint grid codes on a toy trajectory over hexagon-lattice tiles. D shows the T-maze, the field of view and the closed agent loop in colours matching B.
summary_zh: 论文提出多脑区模型 Vector-HaSH+：网格细胞、海马与感觉皮层组成记忆回路，驱动 RNN 策略在 T 迷宫中累积证据。图一四面板：A 原回路，B 带编号连线的新回路，C 联合与分离网格编码对比，D 强化学习闭环。
notes: Prior labels corrected: side-by-side-contrast (C, joint vs disjoint) and actor-interaction (D, agent loop) added; sample data is simulated rate maps and a maze picture, not none. Much of A, C and D is placed as bitmaps with live text on top. The meaning of the black up arrow beside the start region in D and of the N symbols in A is not stated in the supplied text.
